name: Access review population incomplete
description: The entitlement population subject to review omitted part of the in-scope identity estate, commonly service accounts, shared accounts, contractors, privileged roles, or systems fronted by a secondary identity provider. The review may have been performed well over a population that was never complete.

may_assert: That specific identities present in an authoritative source were absent from the reviewed population.
That the reviewed scope is narrower than the scope the control is described as covering.
must_not_assert: That the population is incomplete solely because its generation method was not stated. That is insufficient evidence, not a demonstrated gap.
That every identity class must be in a single review. Separate reviews with their own records are equally valid.

escalates_to.when: The process itself has no step that would ever bring the omitted population into scope, making the omission structural rather than incidental.

de_escalates_to.when: Only detection signal SIG-004 fires: the population generation method is unstated, so completeness can be neither confirmed nor refuted.

severity_factors.criterion_impact: Entitlements outside the population were never assessed, so the control does not cover the scope it is described as covering.
severity_factors.pervasiveness: Omitting one low-risk application differs from omitting all non-human identities.
severity_factors.detectability: Detectable only if the population is reconciled to an authoritative source; otherwise invisible.
escalates_when: Omitted population includes privileged or administrative accounts
The system description claims a coverage the population does not support
de_escalates_when: The omitted population is covered by a separate documented review
The omitted system is genuinely outside the declared system boundary

detection_signals.signal: Reviewed population does not reconcile to the identity provider or HR record count for the same date.
No service accounts or administrative roles appear anywhere in the reviewed population.
Respondent does not select service accounts or privileged roles as included populations.
Evidence does not state how the population was generated, so completeness cannot be assessed.

auditor_impact: Population completeness is assessed before sampling. An unreconcilable population commonly causes the evidence to be rejected and re-requested, and can escalate to a scope limitation if it cannot be established.
customer_impact: Assurance about entitlement appropriateness applies only to the accounts that were actually looked at, which the report does not disclose.
false_positive_guidance: Not a gap where the omitted identities are covered by a separate review with its own record.
Not a gap where a count difference is explained by timing between exports taken on different dates.
Not a gap where the omitted system is outside the declared system boundary; confirm the boundary before flagging.
Service accounts governed by a distinct non-human identity control are covered, not omitted.

source_refs.supports: Population completeness as a precondition to sampling and a frequent cause of evidence rejection.

notes: DriftGuard finding archetype; not an audit finding.
